title: Wikipedia (cocktail articles)
notable_for: Relays IBA official-cocktail specs; tier 3 by PHG convention as a secondary, non-professional reference
rights_note: Specs recorded as facts only; CC BY-SA text not copied

name: David A. Embury
known_for: The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks (1948)

name: Daiquiri (Embury 8:2:1)
steps: Shake rum, lime and syrup hard with ice.
Fine strain into a chilled coupe; lime wedge garnish.

variants.name: Difford's 6:2:1 formula
variants.change: sweeter/tarter 6:2:1 ratio of rum:lime:syrup; amounts not captured

notes: Ratio attributed by Difford's to Embury's The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks (1948); creator_key points to Embury as the author of the formula, not the drink.

name: Daiquiri (Difford's 10:3:2)

lines.note: 10 ml; omit if ice is wet

steps: Stir everything in the shaker base first so the sugar is fully dissolved.
Add ice, shake hard, fine strain into a chilled coupe.

variants.name: Powdered sugar
variants.change: replace sugar syrup with two slightly heaped 5 ml spoons of powdered sugar (level spoons for a tarter drink)

notes: Rum-heavy formula recommended for dry light white rum.

name: Hemingway Daiquiri
steps: Shake everything with ice 15-20 seconds, adding a small piece of grapefruit peel to the tin (regal shake).
Strain into a chilled cocktail glass; very thin lime wheel.

variants.name: PUNCH alternate spec
variants.change: 3/4 oz lime, 1/2 oz grapefruit, 1/2 oz rich 2:1 cane syrup, 1/4 oz Luxardo maraschino; rum amount not captured

notes: Winner of a PUNCH blind tasting of 11 bartender specs. Modern versions add syrup and more grapefruit/maraschino than the Floridita original; see rx_papa_doble.

name: Hemingway Special Daiquiri (Papa Doble)
steps: Shake with ice.
Fine strain into a chilled glass.

variants.name: IBA spec (via Wikipedia)
variants.change: 60 ml rum, 40 ml grapefruit, 15 ml maraschino, 15 ml lime; no syrup

variants.name: El Floridita spec (via Wikipedia)
variants.change: 90 ml light Cuban rum, 5 ml maraschino, 30 ml grapefruit, 15 ml lime; blended about five seconds with crushed ice

notes: Double-strength, unsweetened original made for Hemingway at El Floridita; later specs add syrup.

name: Daiquiri No. 3
steps: Shake with ice.
Strain into an ice-filled glass; lime wedge. The original was blended and served frappé.

variants.name: Original service
variants.change: blended with crushed ice and served frappé instead of on the rocks

sources.locator: excerpt read via WebSearch 2026-09-29; page seen, amounts not captured

notes: Third of four numbered daiquiris in the 1934 Bar La Florida menu booklet; year is Difford's 'circa 1915'.

name: Hotel Nacional Special
steps: Shake with ice until chilled.
Strain into a chilled coupe.

variants.name: Difford's
variants.change: 1.23 oz (as shown) light gold rum, 1/2 oz Luxardo Apricot, 3/4 oz pineapple, 1/2 oz lime, 1/4 oz Monin cane syrup

notes: Hotel bar opened 1930; creator attributed to Eddie Woelke or Wil P. Taylor (uncertain), so creator_key left null. Both sources agree on structure, disagree on rum/pineapple amounts.

name: Sidecar
steps: Shake with ice.
Fine strain into a chilled coupe.

variants.name: 1922 equal parts
variants.change: 1 part brandy, 1 part triple sec, 1 part lemon (earliest published form)

variants.name: Difford's Pineau version
variants.change: adds Pineau des Charentes blanc; amounts not captured

notes: Embury called the equal-parts form too sweet and framed the Sidecar as a brandy Daiquiri with Cointreau as sweetener. Liquor.com/Serious Eats not reachable by the search tool.

name: Brandy Crusta
steps: Rub the glass rim with lemon and dip in powdered sugar; line the inside with a long strip of lemon zest.
Mix ingredients with crushed ice in a tumbler, strain into the prepared glass.
garnish: sugar crust, long lemon zest strip, cherry

variants.name: IBA spec (via Wikipedia)
variants.change: 52.5 ml brandy, 7.5 ml Luxardo maraschino, 1 barspoon curaçao, 15 ml lemon, 1 barspoon simple syrup, 2 dashes aromatic bitters; shaken, sugar-rimmed cocktail glass

variants.name: PUNCH method
variants.change: shaken and strained into sugar-rimmed cocktail glass, peel of half a lemon; amounts not captured

sources.locator: excerpt read via WebSearch 2026-09-29; method/garnish only

notes: Ancestor of the Sidecar. Difford's lists the historic mixing-glass form.

name: Whiskey Sour (no egg)
steps: Shake whiskey, lemon and syrup with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe, or over ice in a rocks glass.

sources.locator: excerpt read via WebSearch 2026-09-29; page seen, amounts not captured

notes: Amounts deliberately null: no attributable no-egg spec surfaced in excerpts. Commonly cited 2:1:1 ratio seen only in unattributed excerpt. See rx_whiskey_sour_egg for a sourced spec.

name: Whiskey Sour with egg white (Boston Sour)
steps: Dry shake everything without ice.
Add four Kold-Draft cubes and shake until cold.
Fine strain into a coupe.
notes: PUNCH names the egg-white form a Boston Sour and uses it as its preferred Whiskey Sour.

name: New York Sour
steps: Shake whiskey, lemon, syrup and egg white with ice.
Strain over fresh ice in a rocks glass.
Float the wine over the back of a barspoon.

variants.name: Common oz spec
variants.change: 2 oz rye, 1 oz lemon, 1/2 oz simple, 1/2 oz red wine float; egg optional

sources.locator: excerpt read via WebSearch 2026-09-29; page seen, amounts not captured

notes: No tier-1/2 spec with amounts surfaced; the oz spec was seen only on blogs alongside Wikipedia, so tagged to Wikipedia with low confidence. Gap.

name: Pisco Sour
steps: Shake with egg white (dry and with ice).
Strain into a chilled glass; dot bitters on the foam.

variants.name: Difford's ratio
variants.change: 3 parts Peruvian pisco (half Italia, half Quebranta or Acholado), 1 lime, 3/4 gomme or sugar syrup, 1/2 egg white; Amargo Chuncho or Angostura drops

variants.name: Difford's split citrus
variants.change: 2 oz pisco, 1/2 oz lime, 1/4 oz lemon, 1/2 oz sugar syrup, 1/2 oz egg white; shake with ice, strain back, dry shake, fine strain

variants.name: Wikipedia standard
variants.change: 60 ml pisco, 30 ml lemon, 20 ml simple syrup, 1 egg white, Amargo bitters garnish

notes: Difford's uses a reverse dry shake (ice first, then dry).

name: Amaretto Sour (Jeffrey Morgenthaler)
steps: Dry shake to emulsify the egg white.
Shake again with ice and strain.

variants.name: Bourbon choice
variants.change: Old Grand-Dad 114 named as acceptable alternative to Booker's

lines.note: bottled or house cordial; see pr_lime_cordial_morgenthaler

steps: Stir gin and lime cordial in the serving glass; ice optional.

name: Margarita
steps: Rim the glass with lime and fine sea salt first.
Shake with ice, strain into an ice-filled glass.

variants.name: Difford's on the rocks
variants.change: adds about 1/6 oz (5 ml) agave syrup for balance

notes: Difford's dates the 2:1:1 proportions to 1937. Liquor.com not reachable by the search tool.

name: Tommy's Margarita
steps: Shake with ice.
Strain over fresh ice; lime wedge.
